text:
acme_ops: Hey folks — after we cut over to a PrivateLink interface endpoint (attached to our TGW) our production app started seeing intermittent 401s and occasional TLS handshake resets to api.redwood.com. Cutover was ~2024-11-03 10:00 UTC. Can someone help escalate? Repro below.

acme_ops: Repro steps: curl from app container -> our proxy -> vpce -> redwood. Example curl:
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.com:443:10.0.5.25 https://api.redwood.com/health -H 'Authorization: Bearer <short-lived token>'
* Connected to 10.0.5.25 (10.0.5.25) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* TLS alert, close notify (SSL3_ST_CLNT_HELLO)
* Received HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_token"}
```
We also see failures where curl returns TLS handshake errors (reset). This is intermittent across requests.

maria_support: Thanks — we'll triage. Two quick asks: 1) can you paste output of `dig +short api.redwood.com @<vpce-resolver-ip>` from a host that fails? 2) can you run an `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.25:443 -servername api.redwood.com -brief` from the same host and paste the handshake summary?

acme_ops: dig returns 10.0.5.25 (private hosted zone -> vpce). openssl snippet:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Let'sEncrypt, CN = R3
verify return:1
---
Server certificate:
 subject=CN = api.redwood.com
 issuer=CN = R3
---
SSL-Session:
 Protocol  : TLSv1.3
 Cipher    : TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
 Verify return code: 0 (ok)
---
```
But tcpdump of the same flow shows a few ClientHello packets with no SNI (or SNI empty) and then RST from backend.

jen_sre: Empty/missing SNI in ClientHello is interesting — that would cause the backend NLB/ALB to select a default cert which could trigger name mismatch or connection reset depending on listener. Where is TLS termination happening? At Redwood (passthrough to model servers) or at our edge ALB?

alex_m: Redwood hosted endpoints observe SNI-based routing and also expect Host header for routing and auth token audience checks. If a proxy rewrites Host or strips SNI, you can see auth/token validation fail or TLS resets.

maria_support: Can you confirm whether your sidecar/proxy is doing TLS origination or TLS passthrough? If the proxy terminates TLS then re-initiates to the vpce, check that it forwards `Host` and sets SNI (`server_name`) on upstream connections. Envoy config often needs `upstream_server_name: "%REQ(:authority)%"` or similar.

acme_ops: We use a corporate sidecar (envoy) that terminates TLS from clients then mTLS to our proxy cluster, then connects to vpce. We found our upstream cluster config had `sni: \"\"` for the redwood route (legacy placeholder).

maria_support: That would explain missing SNI. Quick tests you can run from a failing pod:
```
# show SNI present
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.25:443 -servername api.redwood.com 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,20p'
# raw tcpdump to confirm: (on host)
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.0.5.25 and port 443 -c 50 -w /tmp/vpce.pcap
```
If SNI is missing, the VPCE/NLB will pick default listener/cert. That can cause either TLS handshake drop (if backend rejects) or valid TLS but wrong cert causing client validation failures.

acme_ops: We also posted a `curl -v` directly from an EC2 in same subnet bypassing our proxy: it succeeded consistently. So that points to our proxy.

jen_sre: Other things to check in parallel: security groups on the vpce ENI (ingress from your proxy SG allowed?), and NACLs allowing ephemeral ports (1024-65535) for return traffic. If ephemeral ports are blocked intermittently you'll see TCP resets or half-open TLS.

acme_ops: SGs looked OK (443 open from proxy SG). NACL had a deny on ephemeral range (company-wide policy) — we relaxed to allow ephemeral 1024-65535 and re-tested: some TLS resets dropped but 401s persisted.

alex_m: 401s likely from token/audience mismatch. Can you capture the upstream request headers as seen by Redwood (we can pull logs if you give us request ids)? Also confirm your proxy preserves the `Authorization` header and does not rewrite `Host`. Some proxies replace host header with the vpce DNS name (10.0.5.25) unless configured to preserve. Our token audience check expects host/api.redwood.com.

acme_ops: We searched our proxy logs — found lines where `:authority` was set to the ENI IP for some requests. Envoy cluster config was using `cluster.name` as upstream host.

maria_support: Recommended fixes: 1) set upstream SNI to `%REQ(:authority)%` (or `api.redwood.com`) in proxy config; 2) ensure `preserve_host_header`/`set_host` is disabled so Host remains `api.redwood.com`; 3) allow ephemeral ports in NACL/SG egress; 4) test with `curl --header 'Host: api.redwood.com' --resolve api.redwood.com:443:10.0.5.25 ...` to simulate.

acme_ops: We applied the Envoy change to set `upstream_server_name: "%REQ(:authority)%"` and disabled host rewrite. Also updated NACL. After rollout: within 15m error rate dropped to zero. We replayed 10k requests, no TLS resets, no 401s.

infra-bot: Deploy succeeded: envoy-sidecar-config v2.4.1 -> v2.4.2 (sha: abc123).

maria_support: Great — can you confirm if we can close this ticket? Any postmortem notes you'd like us to add (we can annotate docs about "common proxy misconfigs with PrivateLink")?

acme_ops: Please add note: when using PrivateLink+TGW and sidecar proxies, ensure SNI and Host preservation to avoid auth and TLS issues. Thanks for the quick help! :tada:

jen_sre: Adding to internal KB: "vpce + proxy gotchas: SNI, host-header, ephemeral ports, NACLs, SG routing". Closing after 24h of zero-error. :thumbsup:
